title: Why Does Character Matter More Than Gifting in Ministry?
subtitle: Your gifting gets you the platform, and your character decides whether you survive it, which is the one thing no search committee on earth can measure.
group: The Inner Life of the Leader

sections.title: The Two Things That Grow at Different Speeds
sections.body:
Gifting is fast. Character is slow. A man can develop a remarkable preaching gift in five years and a reliable character in twenty-five, and the gap between those two timelines is where most ministry disasters live.

I have watched it happen. A young man with a real gift, lifted early, praised constantly, handed influence his character had not yet grown into. The gift ran ahead and the character could not keep up, and for a while no one noticed, because a crowd does not interview your marriage. A crowd does not see how you treat the waitress or whether you tell the truth when the truth costs you. A crowd sees the gift, and the gift was genuine, and that is exactly the problem.

Gifting is what you can do. Character is what you are when no one is watching you do it. The first builds the platform. The second determines whether the platform becomes a place of ministry or a place of falling. And the higher the platform, the farther the fall, because the gift that lifted you that high also exposed you to pressures that would have crushed a slower, smaller ascent.

The gift opens the door. Character decides what walks through it.

sections.title: What No Search Committee Can See
sections.body:
A search committee can measure the sermon. It can check the references, watch the videos, count the years. It can assess the gift with real accuracy.

It cannot measure whether you lie in small ways. It cannot see how you spend the afternoon you told everyone was study. It cannot watch you with your children when you are tired and the day went badly. It cannot know whether you are kind to the people who can do nothing for you, which is the truest test of a man there is. The committee evaluates the visible, because the visible is all it has, and the visible is the gift.

This is why the Pastoral Epistles spend almost no words on gifting and almost all of them on character. Read the qualifications in First Timothy three and Titus one and notice what is missing. Eloquence is barely there. Strategic vision is absent. What fills the list is character, almost entirely. Above reproach. Not violent but gentle. Not a lover of money. Manages his own household. Hospitable. Self-controlled. These are not skills. These are the slow growth of a life, and the New Testament treats them as the actual qualification, with one mention of teaching ability tucked in among them.

God weighted the list toward the thing the committee cannot test. He knew which one breaks first.

sections.title: How Gifting Hides a Rotting Character
sections.body:
Here is the cruel mechanism, and I have felt it work in me.

The more gifted you are, the longer you can get away with it. A mediocre man with a character problem is exposed early, because he has nothing to hide behind. A gifted man with the same problem is protected by the gift. People excuse him. They make allowances. He is so anointed, they say, and the word anointed becomes a shield held up in front of a rotting thing. The gift buys him time, and he uses the time not to repair the character but to grow the gift, because the gift is what gets the applause and the character work gets none.

So the gap widens. The platform rises. The character stays where it was, or quietly erodes, because secret sin always erodes, and one day the two are so far apart that any pressure at all snaps the thing in half. The affair. The embezzlement. The cruelty finally seen. And everyone says they never saw it coming, and they are telling the truth, because the gift was facing them the whole time and the character had its back to the wall in the dark.

The gift does not save you. The gift is what kept you from being saved sooner.

sections.title: Tending the Slow Thing on Purpose
sections.body:
If character is slow, then it must be tended deliberately, or the fast thing will outrun it every time. Here is how, concretely.

Get people in your life who are not impressed by your gift. A wife who saw you fail. Old friends who knew you before the title and will laugh at you. An elder board that is not afraid of you. The gift insulates you from correction, so you must build correction back in by hand, on purpose, with people who have permission and the spine to use it.

Do the small honest thing when the small dishonest thing would never be caught. Return the extra change. Correct the flattering story before it spreads. Admit the mistake no one noticed. Character is not built in the crisis. It is built in ten thousand unwatched moments, and the crisis only reveals which way those moments trained you to lean.

Guard the unseen life with more care than the seen one, because the unseen is load-bearing. If your prayer is dying while your preaching improves, stop and attend to the prayer, even if the preaching gets worse for a season. A diminished gift on a solid character is safe. A growing gift on a dying character is a building waiting for weather.

Feed the slow thing daily. The fast thing will feed itself.

sections.title: Finishing, Not Peaking
sections.body:
The goal of a ministry is not to peak. It is to finish.

We celebrate the peak. The big year, the full room, the gift at full stretch. But Scripture does not celebrate peaking. Paul, near the end, does not say I built the largest thing. He says I have finished the race, I have kept the faith. The verb is to finish, and finishing is a character word, not a gift word. Plenty of gifted men start. The question the last day asks is whether you kept the faith, kept the marriage, kept the integrity, all the way to the line.

I have buried gifted men who did not finish, and I have buried plain men who did, and I can tell you which funeral I would rather have. The plain man who finished left a church that still trusts pastors. The gifted man who fell left a wound in everyone who ever believed him.

So tend the slow thing. It is the only part of you that the platform cannot lift, and the only part that will still be standing when the gift is gone.

The gift will fade. The character is what they bury, and what they remember.
